# Results

## The article is already a strong noun lever

With the intervention off, inserting `an` versus `a` moves the
full-vocabulary noun distribution by TV \(0.937\) \([0.891,0.975]\) on
the 20 held-out prompts. A transformers-only baseline, with no sparse
intervention, gives TV \(0.940\) \([0.893,0.976]\) on the same 20 prompts
and TV \(0.975\) \([0.964,0.983]\) on 95 released `an`-target occupations;
the top-1 noun changes on every prompt in both splits. Any sparse handle
that flips the article therefore has a large, generic continuation
channel available before leftover internal control is considered.

## Free generation looks coordinated; the six cells split it

Amplifying S1 at \(5\times\) moves every held-out prompt to `an` and
changes the greedy noun on 19/20 prompts (@tbl-packaging). Concrete twins
include `a pilot`\(\rightarrow\)`an aviator` and
`a lawyer`\(\rightarrow\)`an attorney`. Matched random features and S3 do
not produce this switch. Those free-generation rates show that S1 is a
specific handle on legal article--noun completions. They do not identify
the transmission route.

| Condition | \(N\) | \(\Delta\) art.\ logit favors `an` | Noun token preserved | Class shift | Wrapper-like | Package-like | Twin match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S1 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 1.00 | 0.05 | 0.95 | 0.00 | 0.95 | 0.35 |
| S1 matched control | 20 | 0.70 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| S3 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 0.70 | 0.95 | 0.05 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.00 |

: Free-generation metrics (held-out occupations). Wrapper-like = generated
article moves and noun token stays; package-like = legal article--class
switch. These rates do not identify leftover noun control.
{#tbl-packaging}

The six-cell split does. S1 at \(5\times\) selects `an` on 20/20 prompts.
Inserting that treated article with the intervention **off** reproduces
the S1-on top-1 noun on 20/20 prompts. Across all 20 prompts, total TV is
\(0.893\), token-substitution TV is \(0.891\), and matched-prefix leftover
TV is \(0.028\) \([0.021,0.035]\) (@tbl-mediation; @fig-mediation A).
Cosine of \(E_M\) with \(E_T\) is \(0.949\) \([0.849,1.000]\); cosine of
\(E_R\) with \(E_T\) is \(0.124\) \([-0.112,0.355]\). Reconstruction
\(\|E_T-(E_M+E_R)\|_1\) is numerically zero (implementation check).
Frozen attention in the original S1 factorial yields the same qualitative
split.

| Attention | Total TV | Token-substitution TV | Leftover TV under treated article | Treated-token top-1 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Recomputed (primary) | 0.893 | 0.891 | 0.028 [0.021, 0.035] | 1.00 |
| Frozen (ablation) | 0.893 | 0.891 | 0.026 [0.020, 0.033] | 1.00 |

: S1 \(5\times\) six-cell split on all 20 held-out prompts. Intervals are
prompt-bootstrap 95\% intervals.
{#tbl-mediation}

The leftover is not exactly zero, and it is not confined to the treated
article. On seven listed twins, target-minus-source \(\Delta\Delta\) is
\(0.018\) \([-0.071,0.107]\) under inserted `a` and \(0.089\)
\([0.027,0.152]\) under inserted `an`. Individual `an` leftovers are
pilot\(\to\)aviator \(+0.125\), lawyer\(\to\)attorney \(+0.062\),
physicist\(\to\)astronomer \(+0.062\), photographer\(\to\)artist
\(-0.062\), psychologist\(\to\)anthropologist \(+0.125\),
geologist\(\to\)archaeologist \(+0.250\), farmer\(\to\)agriculturist
\(+0.062\). Free-generation target/source contrast on the same twins is
about \(11.6\) logits; treated-article insertion alone contributes about
\(11.6\) logits (post-hoc descriptive).

![S1 vector split against the generic article lever, and six-cell leftovers across handles and S1 dose.](manuscript/figures/fig_mediation_decomposition.png){#fig-mediation width=94%}

## Dose: the large total effect is gain-gated; the leftover is not

At \(1.5\times\), S1 writes `an` on only \(2/20\) prompts and total TV
collapses to \(0.065\). The leftover under inserted `an` is already
present: TV \(0.015\) and twin \(\Delta\Delta\) \(0.098\)
\([0.027,0.161]\). At \(3\times\), free `an` rises to \(0.90\), total TV
to \(0.802\), and token substitution still dominates (cosine of \(E_M\)
with \(E_T\) remains high). The dramatic free-generation rewrite is
therefore gated by whether the gain is large enough to engage the
article boundary of TV \(0.937\). The small leftover under `an` is not
created only by \(5\times\).

## Family comparison: only S1 produces a large article-flipping rewrite

@tbl-family compares \(5\times\) handles; @fig-mediation B also shows S1 dose.
Only S1 produces a large free-generation article+noun switch, and that switch
remains token-substitution dominated. S3, the attribution-selected
content-ish set, does not move nouns (total TV \(0.025\); noun-changed
rate \(0\)). Attribution future-token scores therefore did not predict
matched-prefix leftover control. S4 never writes `an`. S2 never writes
`an` either; greedy strings often derail (`called a \ldots`,
`not a biologist`), so the 0.70 ``noun changed'' rate is a parse artifact
rather than a coordinated rewrite. S2's leftover TV under `an` is larger
(\(\approx 0.10\)) and its twin \(\Delta\Delta\) under `an` is
\(+0.830\); we do not read that as a content plan. S2 includes a feature
shared with S1 and appears to disrupt continuation, not to transmit a
noun. The S1 leftover under `an` (\(+0.089\)) overlaps the random control
(\(+0.071\) \([0.027,0.134]\)). We therefore do not claim a specific noun
plan from the residual.

| Handle | Free an | Noun changed | Treated top-1 | Total TV | Token-subst. TV | Leftover TV (an) | Twin \(\Delta\Delta\) a | Twin \(\Delta\Delta\) an |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S1 \(5\times\) | 1.00 | 0.95 | 1.00 | 0.893 | 0.891 | 0.028 | 0.018 | 0.089 |
| S2 \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.70 | 0.86 | 0.109 | 0.000 | 0.101 | 0.018 | 0.830 |
| S3 \(5\times\) | 0.05 | 0.00 | 1.00 | 0.025 | 0.000 | 0.021 | 0.062 | 0.018 |
| S4 \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.35 | 1.00 | 0.028 | 0.000 | 0.021 | \(-0.107\) | 0.080 |
| Random \(5\times\) | 0.05 | 0.05 | 1.00 | 0.019 | 0.000 | 0.020 | 0.000 | 0.071 |

: Six-cell family sweep at \(5\times\) on the same 20 held-out prompts. S2/S4 noun-changed rates often reflect illegal greedy strings. S2's vector split is defined only on prompts whose free articles are a or an.
{#tbl-family}

## Propagation, residual reference, and synthetic polarity

Applying S1 at \(P\) changes sparse CLT activations one token later at
the inserted-article position beginning at layer 11 (mean activation
\(\Delta L_2\) \(11.6\) at layer 11, \(133.8\) at layer 12). Mean noun TV
on these four diagnostics is \(0.025\). The leftover is therefore
architecturally reachable.

A full-residual patch at the inserted-article position validates
stack sensitivity. Layer 12 is selected on four development pairs. On
four held-out same-article-class pairs, the target-specific effect is
\(+6.44\) logits \([4.19,10.06]\), versus \(+0.14\) \([-0.33,0.61]\) for
ten matched-norm random directions averaged within pair
(@tbl-reference). Earlier MLP-input patches at \(P\) failed to move nouns
(Appendix E).

| Intervention | Held-out \(N\) | Mean target-specific \(\Delta\Delta\) [95\%] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Layer-12 target residual | 4 | \(6.44\) [4.19, 10.06] |
| Matched-norm random residual | 4 | \(0.14\) [\(-0.33,0.61\)] |

: Development-selected full-residual reference. This validates
sensitivity of noun computation to an upstream state; it does not show
that S1 contains the same information.
{#tbl-reference}

On two known generative mechanisms (Appendix G), the same estimands
return leftover TV \(0\) for article-only mediation and leftover TV
\(0.667\) under inserted `a` for a persistent plan bias. The Gemma
full-residual reference remains the stack-sensitivity control; the
synthetic pair shows that the estimands are not biased toward declaring
token substitution.
